getting-started.html.title: Your first clip
getting-started.html.heading: Your first clip
getting-started.html.description: Get one short shot working. Add continuity, refinement or delivery processing only when you need it.

sections.title: Before you touch a setting
sections.body:
A workflow is a set of connected nodes. Left sockets accept data; right sockets return it. MODEL carries weights, IMAGE carries pictures, and AUDIO carries a waveform. Matching types matter.

The starter already connects the core pieces. Select installed files, author a clip and run through its connected Smart Preview. You do not run every box separately.

In the node menu, Master and Director Settings are under ComfyUI-AhmedAhmedEG → Start here; Reference Pack is under References and prompts; Smart Preview is under Output. The guide navigation groups tools by learning task.

sections.title: 1. Load the right model family
sections.body:
Keep both diffusion families connected. FL2VA serves compatible text, image and endpoint tasks. REF2VA serves reference-guided and video-editing tasks. The Master chooses the family needed by each clip.

Select the MiniMax text encoder with loader type minimax, the H3 video VAE and the H3 audio VAE. These files live on the ComfyUI server, not merely on your laptop.

An upstream Turbo LoRA/model switch can change the model and its expected step schedule. Keep them consistent. Clip-local LoRAs add their own patches; removing a clip entry cannot undo a patch already present on the input model.

sections.title: 2. Choose a small first test
sections.body:
Use Director Settings for output size, initial steps, sampler and schedule. H3 sampling runs at 24 fps and uses a 32-pixel canvas grid. Both 1280 and 1344 are divisible by 32; they are different valid widths.

A 320 × 192, two-step test checks wiring quickly; it is not suitable for judging final quality. Use your intended model schedule and canvas for a quality comparison. Saved starter values can differ from a newly added node’s defaults.

Keep optional SelfLift, Refine, Face Refine, Semantic Bridge and residual Cache disconnected for a baseline. Keep decoded_output=latest for normal preview work.

sections.title: 3. Prepare inputs, then assign them
sections.body:
Connect loader outputs into Reference Pack. Edit one asset at a time with Edit Reference. Native VIDEO carries its own timing and may carry sound. An IMAGE frame batch needs its source FPS and paired audio supplied separately.

On the Master clip choose the task, then assign only the needed prepared assets. An asset’s role label helps prompt writing; it does not automatically wire an opening/ending frame.

sections.title: 4. Write a focused shot and run
sections.body:
1. Describe the subject, action, camera and sound. Insert the clip’s current Picture/Video tokens rather than inventing reference numbers.
  2. Choose a short duration, a fixed seed and Independent continuity for the first clip.
  3. Choose Next clip to generate one eligible result, or All clips for the eligible sequence.
  4. Watch the active generation animation, then inspect Latest clip. Approve only a usable result you want reused.

sections.title: 5. Continue deliberately
sections.body:
Add or duplicate the next clip, describe its next action beat and choose a continuity method. Motion Context uses native previous audiovisual guides where compatible. Latent Carry copies a tail with tapered redraw masks. FL2VA Tail Handoff uses a final-frame opening handoff.

Video and audio context are independent: 22 frames is about 0.92 seconds, 24 frames is one second, and 56 frames is about 2.33 seconds at 24 fps. Borrowed context adds work and is removed from delivered new frames.

Duration = new footage describes the visible addition. Duration includes context (Extender) describes the sampling window, so the delivered segment is shorter after prefix removal.

sections.title: 6. Review, reuse and export
sections.body:
The yellow outline selects an editor target. A saved-result indicator means files exist. Approval asks the Master to reuse a result. Unapproving preserves its files and clears continuity-dependent later approvals; successful regeneration replaces the current result.

Smart Preview updates during the run as clips finish. Its Full video scope is separate from Director Settings decoded_output. For a full cached sequence, use Project Video. Video Combine encodes only the frames and audio you feed it.

sections.title: Words you will meet
sections.body:
Clip
One timeline item.
Latent / VAE
Compressed working data / the encoder-decoder that converts it to and from visible or audible media.
Checkpoint
A completed cached clip here, not a paused sampler state or diffusion model file.
Seed
Starting randomness; one part of a reproducible setup.
Conditioning
Prompt, assigned references and supported continuity guidance.
Refine
Extra processing after the initial generation; it can change the result.
Megapixels
A spatial pixel budget, not duration or a frame-count limit.
Approval
Request to reuse a current available result during generation.
Preview stage
A current result’s first pass or refinement stage, not an older generation.

workflows.html.title: Practical workflows
workflows.html.heading:
One change.
One clear purpose.
workflows.html.description: Recipes that put a setting in its correct place and tell you what to inspect afterwards.

sections.title: Continue an action
sections.body:
Set it up

Keep the first clip’s settings as a baseline. On the next clip choose Motion Context, a short video context and an independent audio context. Use New footage duration for the intended visible addition.

Check the result

Inspect the seam, action and sound. More context adds work; it cannot guarantee exact choreography. Latent Carry is a different masked-prefix method, not a stronger setting of Motion Context.

Open the node chapter →

sections.title: Reduce reference video cost
sections.body:
Set it up

Select the video in Reference Pack → Resize → Megapixels. Start with 0.5 MP. Choose Video Only to exclude the soundtrack or Video + Audio when both belong in conditioning.

Check the result

The pack prepares pixels before native reference encoding. It follows aspect ratio and alignment without enlarging smaller sources; output canvas remains a separate Director setting.

Open the node chapter →

sections.title: Inspect first, refine later
sections.body:
Set it up

Connect Refine and enable Confirm First Pass before generating. Review the first pass, approve that stage on its timeline card, then run again. Use global to retain its audio.

Check the result

A matching staged first pass is reused. Ten completed initial steps plus fifteen refinement steps are not a twenty-five-step initial schedule. Persistent exact sampler resume is not exposed.

Open the node chapter →

sections.title: Compare SelfLift fairly
sections.body:
Set it up

Generate a baseline with SelfLift disconnected. Keep seed, prompt, assets and target canvas unchanged, then connect SelfLift with a learned H3 latent upscaler and choose the low/high-resolution split.

Check the result

Compare faces, hands, action, detail and runtime. A smaller early canvas changes the sampling path; it does not guarantee equivalent or better quality.

Open the node chapter →

sections.title: Use a LoRA on one clip
sections.body:
Set it up

Open that clip’s LoRAs tab. Add an enabled compatible H3 patch and set its model strength. Keep other variables fixed.

Check the result

Check upstream model patches too. A globally patched input and a clip-local patch can both apply. Same seed alone is not a controlled comparison.

Open the node chapter →

sections.title: Draft several shots
sections.body:
Set it up

Configure a Prompt Forge provider. Request a small number of focused shots and review its proposal before append/replace.

Check the result

The output is text, not rendered video. Roles/cast help writing; clip asset assignment separately owns video model conditioning. External providers receive submitted context.

Open the node chapter →

sections.title: Export all current clips
sections.body:
Set it up

Connect Master.project_state to Project Video. Choose final, all and the correct FPS. Enable individual shot files if needed.

Check the result

Readable cached media can export without new diffusion. decoded_output=latest does not remove the other cached clips. Exported files remain separate from automatic cache replacement.

Open the node chapter →

sections.title: Reduce an audible join
sections.body:
Set it up

Inspect the generated soundtrack and per-clip Audio Context first. Use project Join Fade for waveform clicks and gain matching for loudness jumps.

Check the result

Fading cannot make unrelated music, changed voices or different ambience semantically continuous. Audio Context affects generation; Join Fade affects assembled output.

Open the node chapter →

architecture.html.title: How the pieces fit
architecture.html.heading: Each setting has a home.
architecture.html.description: Prepare inputs, generate a result, review it, then export it. Change one stage at a time when explaining a difference.

sections.title: From assets to delivery
sections.body:
Loader nodes→Reference Pack
Prepare inputs→Master + Settings
Assign & sample→Current cache→Preview / export

SelfLift is inside initial sampling. Refine runs after the first pass. Face Refine follows the main result. Pixel Upscale and Frame Interpolation process decoded output. Several stages expose size or strength controls because they perform different jobs.

sections.title: Current result, approval and replacement
sections.body:
Each clip has one current generation. Its latent, audio, frames and available current stages live on the server. A replacement publishes after saving succeeds, then superseded generation artifacts are removed. Failed replacement saves retain the old usable current result.

Approval asks Master to reuse a result. Unapproval preserves files while clearing later continuity-dependent approvals. Idle preview shows current completed results without requiring approval. During a run, it follows reused results and newly finished replacements instead of presenting queued old results as fresh completions.

sections.title: Why the same seed can look different
sections.body:
Compare the actual model/LoRAs, attention patches, canvas, steps/sigmas, sampler/scheduler, shifts, effective prompt, asset order and preparation, clip type, continuity method and duration policy. Same prompt and seed alone are insufficient.

Disconnect optional modifiers for a baseline and change one feature at a time. A functional check can prove a setting reaches its processing path; it does not prove aesthetic improvement.

sections.title: Memory and persistence
sections.body:
Current clip data is disk-backed and working resources are released between stages. decoded_output=latest avoids retaining an unnecessary full raw batch; all current results remain available to cached preview/export. Project Video exports clips in sequence. Browser prebuffering is bounded and best effort.

Workflow JSON stores authoring and links, not every generated latent. Portable reference archives, cache data and exported movies are separate artifacts. A completed checkpoint does not preserve an unfinished sampler’s full state.

sections.title: Choose a clip type
sections.body:
TaskAssignmentsPurpose
Existing Video · VIDEOExactly one videoUse existing frames without diffusion; later clips can continue its ending.
Text To Video · T2VNo explicit pool referencesGenerate from text; a separate continuity setting can still supply supported previous context.
Image To Video · I2VOne imageOpening keyframe.
First And Last Frame · FL2VTwo ordered images; continuity can provide the opening handoffOpening and ending keyframes.
Ending Image To Video · L2VOne imageClosing keyframe.
Generate From References · REF2VUp to 9 images, 3 videos, 3 audio; 12 totalNew reference-guided audiovisual content. Audio needs visual conditioning.
Edit Video · V2VExactly one source videoTransform the chosen source range.
Edit Video With References · RV2VFirst selected video is source; reference caps include itEdit source footage with additional references.
Edit Still Image · IMGExactly one imageReturn a single edited image, not a video clip.

Native reference conditioning allows at most 15 seconds per video and 15 seconds of video total, plus at most 15 seconds per audio reference and 15 seconds of audio total. Audio references require visual conditioning. A large chained pool does not increase native per-clip capacity.
